title: Redwood cost economics discovery with Larkridge Capital
summary: Initial cost/unit economics discovery focused on per-token pricing, batching/caching levers, and whether Hosted vs Dedicated makes sense given Larkridge's budget and latency needs. Agreed to share pricing spreadsheet, run a small benchmark on representative prompts, and follow up with security docs for VPC/KMS questions.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Evan (Larkridge Head of ML), Priya (Infra), Marcus (FinOps)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:03] Evan: Yeah good, thanks Maya. Appreciate you fitting us in.
[00:06] Maya: Of course. Quick intro - I'm Maya on the account side, Jonah is our solutions engineer. We wanted to focus this call on cost/unit economics - per-token pricing and the levers you can pull like batching, KV cache, quantization, also tradeoffs between Hosted and Dedicated. Is that the right framing?
[00:23] Evan: That's perfect. Marcus will mainly care about cost but Priya's concerned about isolation and KMS.
[00:29] Jonah: Great, can I ask a few quick qualification q's? Rough token volume, typical sequence lengths, and percent of responses that need sub-200ms latency?
[00:38] Priya: Sure. Right now we're prototyping - maybe 50k to 200k tokens per day over the next quarter, but if the pilot goes well we expect to scale to 5-8M tokens/day within 6 months. Median request is 120 tokens input, 80 tokens output. Latency SLO varies by route: critical routes want <200ms p50, others are fine with 500-800ms.
[01:02] Marcus: Budget wise, we're targeting <$8k/month for the initial pilot, but willing to consider reserved capacity if the unit economics justify it.
[01:10] Jonah: Ok. So high level, Hosted gives simplest onboarding with per-token pricing and no infra to manage. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale via reserved GPU pools. Private/VPC is our on-prem/VPC option for strict isolation and KMS integration.
[01:23] Evan: And how does per-token pricing actually break down - CPU/GPU time vs model size vs optimizations like quantization?
[01:31] Jonah: Good q. Our pricing is primarily per-token but it's informed by model family and execution costs - bigger models and longer contexts cost more per token. The levers you mentioned matter: batching amortizes kernel overhead, KV/prefix caching avoids recomputation for repeated contexts, and aggressive quantization reduces GPU memory and can speed throughput which drops cost/ token. We'll send a cost model spreadsheet but rough numbers - hosted might be $0.0008 to $0.003 per token depending on model and latency tier; Dedicated reserved capacity can push down to the low end or lower with committed spend.
[02:03] Marcus: That range is wide. What's realistic for a use case like ours - primarily 13B-class models for summarization and reranking?
[02:12] Jonah: For optimized 13B with 8-bit quantization and batching, you could see ~$0.0009-0.0012 per token on Dedicated at modest commit levels. Hosted will be a bit higher for equivalent latency. But caching can reduce effective tokens billed - if you cache prefixes or KV for repeated prompts you can cut 20-60% depending on pattern.
[02:33] Priya: The caching bit is interesting - our workflows have a lot of shared context: investor templates, company descriptions, same prompt prefixes. How much work to enable prefix/KV caching?
[02:42] Jonah: Minimal - it's built-in. You can opt-in per-route. The nuance is change frequency: if your prefixes change often cache hit rates drop. For seqs with repeated prefixes we commonly see 30-50% token savings.
[02:57] Evan: Alright. Can you explain batching tradeoffs? We worry about batching adding latency to critical routes.
[03:03] Jonah: Absolutely. Continuous batching groups in-flight requests for kernel amortization. You configure batch size and max wait. For critical routes, set low max wait (e.g., 5-10ms) to keep p50 low; you still get some efficiency. For non-critical batches you can tolerate 20-40ms additional queuing for better cost/unit. We can show tradeoff curves from benchmarks.
[03:23] Marcus: So for our pilot, if we target 5M tokens/day and use 13B quantized with caching and moderate batching, ballpark monthly cost?
[03:31] Jonah: Rough calc - 5M tokens * $0.001 per token = $5k/month. With caching you might drop to $3.5-4k. That's Dedicated pricing with a small commit; Hosted could be 15-30% higher. We'll run exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[03:45] Evan: That aligns with Marcus's budget target if we hit caching numbers.
[03:50] Priya: Security - we need KMS integration and audit logs. Hosted can meet SOC 2 but does it support customer-managed keys?
[03:58] Maya: Hosted supports encryption at rest and we have SOC2 reports. Customer-managed KMS is available on Private (VPC) and for Dedicated we support KMS integrations for enterprise customers - we can share the HLD.
[04:11] Priya: Ok, good. Also need VPC peering and egress controls.
[04:15] Jonah: VPC options exist for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be used via private endpoints in some regions but for strict egress controls we typically recommend Dedicated or Private.
[04:25] Evan: One more - what about fallbacks and graceful degradation? If Dedicated is saturated does Redwood automatically route to hosted models?
[04:33] Jonah: Yes, smart routing supports policy-based fallback to compatible model variants or hosted capacity. You configure cost vs latency priorities. We also have autoscaling and burst capacity options.
[04:42] Marcus: Competitors - are there differences vs OpenAI or Lambda Labs on unit economics?
[04:47] Maya: In general OpenAI has a managed simplicity story but Dedicated-like reserved capacity with kernel optimizations or quantization at cadence is where we differentiate - you can get lower unit cost at scale with more control. Lambda Labs is more self-hosted. We'll put a comparison note in the follow-up.
[04:59] Evan: Sounds good. Practical next steps?
[05:02] Maya: Proposed: 1) We'll send a pricing + cost-model spreadsheet with scenarios (hosted/dedicated/private) 2) Jonah will propose a small benchmark plan and parameters to run on your sample prompts 3) We'll share security docs (SOC2, KMS/HLD, network configs) 4) Schedule a 30-min POC kickoff once Marcus approves budget.
[05:19] Marcus: That works. Can you include an estimate for committed vs on-demand costs?
[05:23] Jonah: Yep - we'll include committed discount curves.
[05:25] Priya: I'll share a sample workload and some traces by Friday.
[05:28] Evan: And we'll loop in procurement for contract terms if the numbers look good.
[05:32] Maya: Great. Quick recap - send spreadsheet + docs, benchmark plan, customer shares sample prompts. Any blockers?
[05:39] Evan: No blockers. Timing is tight but doable.
[05:42] Maya: Alright we'll follow up by email and set the POC kickoff. Thanks everyone.

[End of recording - transcription imperfect in spots, some speaker labels may be approximate]
